name: Overpass-the-Hash / Pass-the-Key (Rubeus asktgt)
description: Convert an NTLM hash into a Kerberos TGT using Rubeus. Enables Kerberos-based lateral movement without needing plaintext credentials.

recommended.note: Use injected Kerberos ticket for PS Remoting

notes: /opsec generates RC4 AS-REQ but uses AES for the session key - less suspicious. Prefer AES key if available. runas /netonly starts a process whose network auth uses the supplied account without validating it locally - handy to use captured plaintext/NTLM before/instead of a forged TGT.

defense.why_it_works: Overpass-the-Hash (also called Pass-the-Key) converts an NTLM hash or AES Kerberos key into a fully valid Kerberos TGT using the AS-REQ/AS-REP exchange. Rubeus asktgt takes the hash and requests a TGT from the KDC - which is then injected into the current session via klist or loaded by Rubeus. Unlike PtH (which sends the hash in NTLM challenge-response), OPtH produces a legitimate Kerberos ticket that works everywhere NTLM would be blocked.
defense.prerequisites: An NTLM hash or AES Kerberos key (from LSASS dump or DCSync). Rubeus or Mimikatz. Network access to DC on port 88 (Kerberos). Target account's SPN or service must accept Kerberos authentication.
defense.impact: T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash + T1558.001 Golden Ticket. Impersonates the target user with a valid Kerberos ticket - full access to resources that account can reach. Particularly powerful for DA accounts dumped via DCSync.
defense.detection:
Event 4768 (TGT request) from a workstation/server that doesn't normally request TGTs for that account (anomalous Kerberos AS-REQ source). RC4 encryption type in TGT request when AES is expected (Rubeus with /rc4 flag). MDI: 'Suspected overpass-the-hash attack'. Sysmon Event 10 if combined with LSASS dump. New TGT issued for a DA account from an unexpected host.
Stolen Kerberos tickets or token impersonation: logon sessions from accounts without expected interactive logon events (DET0338/AN0954).
Access tokens or SSH keys used without corresponding login shell or PAM module activity, especially for remote execution (AN0955).
Token replay or impersonation in federated logins without interactive browser session or MFA prompts (AN0956).
OAuth token reuse from different geographic regions without full login events (AN0957).
Container process using mounted cloud credentials or token cache without known orchestration (AN0958).
Access token reuse for SharePoint or Outlook APIs without interactive user context (AN0959).
Instance metadata token use across instances or misuse of short-lived tokens for different roles (AN0960).
defense.artifacts: Event 4768: TGT request for privileged account from unexpected host | MDI alert: 'Suspected overpass-the-hash attack' | Event 4624 logon type 3 or 9 from new source | SIEM: DA Kerberos AS-REQ from workstation
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4768 Ticket_Encryption_Type=0x17
| where match(Account_Name, "(?i)admin")
| table _time, Computer, Account_Name, Client_Address

index=sysmon EventCode=1 CommandLine="*asktgt*" CommandLine="*/rc4*"
| table _time, Computer, User, CommandLine
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4768 and TicketEncryptionType == "0x17"
| join kind=inner (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4768 | summarize baseline=make_set(IpAddress) by TargetUserName) on TargetUserName
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, IpAddress
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
defense.sigma_rules: win_security_overpass_the_hash_rc4 (RC4 TGT for account normally AES), proc_creation_win_hktl_rubeus
defense.prevention:
Credential Guard prevents NTLM hash extraction from LSASS. Protected Users group: tickets can't be delegated and use AES-only (RC4 OPtH fails). Enable AES-only Kerberos on sensitive accounts (Set-ADUser -KerberosEncryptionType AES256). MDI deployment. Require DA accounts to logon only from PAWs - anomalous TGT source detected by SIEM.
Account Use Policies: Restrict authentication material use outside expected contexts.
Active Directory Configuration: Configure AD to prevent certain techniques; use SID Filtering.
Application Developer Guidance: Implement token binding (Azure AD token protection, OAuth DPoP/Proof of Possession) to cryptographically bind tokens.
Audit: Scan for insecure configurations and potential weaknesses.
Password Policies: Set and enforce secure password policies.
Privileged Account Management: Limit credential overlap across systems to reduce lateral movement risk.
User Account Management: Enforce least privilege; prevent domain users from being local admins on multiple systems.
defense.evasion: Use /aes256 flag with AES key instead of RC4 hash - blends with normal AES Kerberos traffic. Inject ticket into a process rather than the current logon session to avoid event correlation. Use from a PAW-adjacent host to avoid source-IP anomaly detection.
defense.misconfiguration: Credential Guard not enabled. Protected Users group not used for DA accounts. RC4 encryption not restricted. No monitoring of DA account TGT requests from unexpected sources. LSASS PPL disabled (allows hash extraction prerequisite).
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Credential Guard NOT enabled:
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard').EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity
# Returns 0 or $null = VBS/Credential Guard disabled = NTLM hashes extractable from LSASS

# Protected Users NOT used for DAs:
Get-ADGroupMember 'Protected Users' | Select-Object Name
# DA accounts not in Protected Users → NTLM hashes delegatable
defense.secure_config:
# Enable Credential Guard:
# Computer Config → Admin Templates → System → Device Guard
# → Turn On Virtualization Based Security: Enabled
# → Credential Guard Configuration: Enabled with UEFI lock

# Add all DA accounts to Protected Users:
Get-ADGroupMember 'Domain Admins' | ForEach-Object {
  Add-ADGroupMember 'Protected Users' $_.distinguishedName
}
# Protected Users: no NTLM, no RC4 Kerberos, no delegation, no cached creds

# Force AES-only Kerberos for sensitive accounts:
Set-ADUser DomainAdmin1 -KerberosEncryptionType AES256

# SIEM alert:
# EventID=4768 AND TicketOptions=0x40800010 (forwardable+renewable+canonicalize)
# AND ServiceName=krbtgt AND ClientAddress NOT IN (known PAW IPs for DA) → ALERT

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Check for credential dumping artifacts (LSASS access, SAM hive reads, Kerberos anomalies)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: runas /netonly (inject creds into a new logon session)

explain:
Turns an NTLM hash into a real Kerberos TGT (overpass-the-hash) for Kerberos lateral movement:
  asktgt                    request a TGT from the KDC
  /user:<user>             the account to authenticate as
  /rc4:<nt_hash>           its NTLM hash used as the Kerberos key (use /aes256 for opsec)
  /domain:<domain>         the domain
  /ptt                      inject the ticket into the current session
  /opsec                    mimic a genuine client's request flags
With the TGT injected you access services (dir \\<dc>\C$) as that user without ever knowing the plaintext.
